title: 22nd Sitting of Second session of 2026
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Fonadhoo); Deputy Speaker Ahmed Saleem (Eydhafushi) took the chair from the middle of question time until the recess, and the Speaker returned afterwards
summary: The sitting opened at 09:05 with routine business, then spent most of the morning on questions to the Minister of Homeland Security, Labour and Technology, Ali Ihsan. Members asked about the release of personal information in police cases, irregular migrants and visas, police station building projects, drugs, gangs, prisons, ID cards and passports, search and rescue, and protest permits. The President's letter on joining the Multinational Maritime Defence Coalition was sent to the Foreign Relations Committee, and the first reading of a bill amending the National Payment System Act was read. Debate on that bill began and was still going when this part ends. The text is readable but some words and numbers are garbled. The second half of the sitting finished the debate on a bill amending the Payment System Act, then turned to two Finance Committee products on the Auditor General's special audit of Fenaka Corporation (2021-2023): a committee report and a resolution calling for faster investigation and action on the corruption it flagged. Members debated the audit findings, and some exchanges became partisan about past and present governments. At the voting time the Payment System bill was accepted and sent to the Finance Committee, and both the Fenaka report and the resolution passed with no votes against. The sitting then adjourned to 12 August 2026.

Vote on the Fenaka corruption-investigation resolution (Madaveli member Mohamed Shameez)

speakers.name: Ali Ihsan
positions: As Homeland Security Minister, said personal information is disclosed only in limited cases and a data privacy bill now in the Majlis will set the rules.
Said police stations are being built across islands with most due by June 2027, and that the migrant problem is being tackled through identity, entry and compliance checks.
Said drug-related places have been closed and larger seizures made, a career portal has launched, and prison capacity is being expanded.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked about progress on finding a person missing after an incident at sea, and what the minister means by resolving the migrant issue.
Asked why work on the B. Kamadhoo police station has not started although the land was handed over, and whether any foreigner may work without a Maldivian sponsor.
In the bill debate, said the dollar shortage is the biggest financial problem; the chair asked him to stay on the bill.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Asked what results the government has seen since the gang crime law passed and what is being done about gang violence.
Said the audit shows large spending without competitive bidding and criticised how the previous government handled Fenaka.
Urged councils to read the report aloud to residents of every island.
On the resolution, said the money trail involved the finance ministry of the time and that responsibility should not rest on one person.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked what action was taken against foreigners working outside the sector their visa allows.
Asked how the ministry will stop foreigners trading in local markets, and what drug-prevention work it does for young people.
Strongly supported the payment bill as a step toward a cashless economy that helps small businesses.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Supported the bill, saying the changes support the digital payment system and the national payment switch.
Presented the Finance Committee report on the Fenaka audit: spending on goods and services outside competitive bidding, and contracts with firms linked to a former managing director's family.
Presented the resolution report, noting loans and advance subsidies given to Fenaka by the finance ministry and a bank, and asked the Majlis to adopt it.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Asked what rules let the government disclose personal messages between police and a victim support service, and when an SOP on releasing personal information will be published.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked when the findings on a ministry fire would be made public, why they are delayed, and how large the loss to the state was.
Asked what action was taken against police named for negligence by a presidential commission, and for an update on probes of the Malé power outage.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked when the Thoddoo police station will be finished, how ready police are for the tourist season, and how many political appointees the ministry has.
Asked how far the death penalty promise has progressed and whether a Majeedhee Magu protest permit was refused for political reasons.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Asked what the results have been since the drug law was amended.
Asked how the ministry matches unemployed young people with employers and what career guidance it offers.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Asked about the current state of prisons, citing past drone drug drops, violence and scams.
Presented the payment system bill, saying it would build a national payment switch and speed up payments to merchants.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Asked about vehicles being impounded for 15 days with a MVR 750 fine, and said many people complain it is applied unevenly.
Said the audit points to a large loss of public money and asked whether it can be recovered through the law, urging that those responsible be prosecuted.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked what the foreign-operated helicopter and Dornier platforms mean for internal security.
Asked about progress on the Maradhoo police station and whether victim support has a mandate to share information.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Asked how far efforts to resolve the cases of migrants living in the country against the rules have progressed.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked whether the migrant issue is under control and how many police stations burned in past unrest are being rebuilt.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Asked whether legal action is possible against people spreading hostility toward police, and about promises on the migrant issue by the previous government.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Asked how far ID card and passport services will reach atoll islands and what benefits they bring.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Asked why police and soldiers keep dying in operations and whether proper procedures are in place.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Asked what the ministry has achieved in extending police services to all islands.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Asked when barricades left on Malé streets for many years would be removed, given traffic and parking problems.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked about the ministry's search and rescue capability, and about a mental health crisis line.

speakers.name: Adam Shafeeq
positions: Asked when police stations in Makunudhoo, Neykurendhoo and Kumundhoo will open and how street vending on pavements will be handled.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked whether foreign workers who fled would be asked why before deportation, and whether sponsors could be spoken to.

speakers.name: Abdulla Sodig
positions: Asked the minister's plan for police staffing and resources in Addu, and the timeline for the Hithadhoo police station.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the Payment System amendment, saying it protects Maldivians from extra charges on domestic transfers and keeps bank details away from scammers; criticised opposition remarks as off-topic.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said the audit shows public money was misused, and called on institutions to recover it and act.
Said this was not the best time to debate it at length and would raise more points on another bill.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Said no enforcement action had followed despite the report, and urged the police and the Anti-Corruption Commission to act on the findings.
Pointed to purchase orders issued only days before goods arrived as an example of what the report shows.

decisions: The chair accepted the minutes of sittings 16 to 18, as no amendments were submitted.
The President's letter on joining the Multinational Maritime Defence Coalition was sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
The first reading of the bill amending the National Payment System Act (Act 2021/8) was read and preliminary debate began.
The sitting went into recess from 10:30 to 11:00.
Debate on the National Payment System Act amendment bill was closed and the bill went to a vote.
The bill to amend the National Payment System Act was accepted 61-0 and sent to the Finance Committee for review.
The Finance Committee report on the Fenaka Corporation special audit passed 63-0.
The resolution calling for faster investigation and action on corruption flagged in the Fenaka audit passed 64-0.
The sitting was adjourned to Wednesday 12 August 2026 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accept the National Payment System Act amendment bill (62 members present)
Finance Committee report on the Fenaka Corporation special audit (64 members present)
Resolution to speed up investigation and action on corruption in the Fenaka audit (65 members present)
